sentence: This project studies how the body controls T cell responses during long-lasting viral infection, so that immunotherapies can work better.
This project studies the molecular and cellular steps that control how therapeutic T cells move toward solid tumors.
This project studies how long-lasting stress signaling changes tumor growth and response to therapy in neuroblastoma, a childhood cancer.
This project studies how shifts in spatial attention change the hippocampal codes for place, using echolocating bats.
This project tries to find out whether a pocket on Integrin Alpha V, needed by colon, pancreatic and breast cancers, can be targeted with a drug.
This project supports research on how to prevent cancer and reduce its harm, from its genetic and environmental causes to screening and survivorship.
This project uses machine learning and genetic studies to better predict how age-related macular degeneration progresses and responds to treatment.
This project studies how serotonin interacts with inhibitory neurons that help control impulsive behavior and cognitive flexibility.
This project tests whether blocking a cancer-driving factor, on which rhabdomyosarcoma cells depend, could work against that cancer.
This project provides statistical and computer support for studies of how social factors, clinical factors and biology relate in endometrial cancer.
This project tries to find out how thermogenic fat, a tissue that burns extra energy, is naturally controlled in the body.
This project studies how a group of kinases controls an injury pathway in retinal ganglion cells, and tests protective strategies in rodent models of glaucoma.
This project builds small-molecule degraders that break down a drug target, to test whether this could treat Mixed-lineage leukemia gene translocations.
This project studies how tumors get and control their supply of nucleotides, and how nucleotides from the diet affect tumor growth.
This project studies which illnesses, genes and other risk factors combine with human leukocyte antigen to make some people react badly to vancomycin.
This project studies how Toll receptors and mitochondrial networks work together to change the shape of epithelial cells as tissue elongates in the embryo.
This project studies how the drug mitotane changes adrenocortical carcinoma tumors so that immunotherapy works better, using human tumor tissue and pre-clinical models.
This project uses single-cell studies in nonhuman primates to find which brain cells harbor the virus and how cocaine and therapy change the brain.
This project studies the gut microbiomes and metabolomes of hospital patients to find how common dysbiosis is and how it relates to antimicrobial resistant infections.
This project studies how fasting protects cells of the small intestine from high dose radiation therapy, so that side effects can be reduced.
